items.title: Phil Collins Inducted Into Rock & Roll Hall of Fame: “You Haven’t Heard the Last from Me”
items.summary:
Phil Collins entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist on Saturday night at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, becoming a two-time inductee after going in with Genesis in 2010. Travis Barker handled the induction speech, and Cynthia Erivo performed in Collins' honor.

Barker, a drummer himself, built his tribute around the sound that made Collins famous. "I remember hearing the drums [for 'In the Air Tonight'] for the first time and being blown away," he said, calling it a sound that "changed everything" and helped define drum recording in the 1980s. He noted that Collins managed a massive solo career while remaining in Genesis: "He wasn't just successful at both, he was one of the best at both."

Collins kept his acceptance brief and characteristically dry. "I grew up wanting to play drums. Everything else has been a happy accident," he said, before telling the room, "you haven't heard the last of me. I promise you that." He also thanked "my three ex wives, because they've loved me through the years and given me five great children." His daughter, Lily Collins, attended the ceremony with him. Erivo then sang "In the Air Tonight" with Barker on drums.

Collins did not perform. As Consequence reported, he had said earlier this year that he passed on the opportunity because he wasn't match-fit enough to rehearse and sing properly, though he left open the possibility of returning to the stage. Nerve damage tied to back problems ended his drumming, and knee surgeries and mobility issues have compounded the difficulty; his son Nic Collins played drums on his later solo tours and the 2021–2022 Genesis farewell run.

The induction lands more than four decades after Collins launched his solo career with 1981's Face Value, followed by Hello, I Must Be Going!, No Jacket Required and But Seriously, and hits including "Against All Odds," "Sussudio," "One More Night" and "Another Day in Paradise." He joined Genesis as drummer in 1970 and took over lead vocals after Peter Gabriel left in 1975.

The rest of the 2026 Performer class includes Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan, with additional honors going to Fela Kuti, Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, Gram Parsons, Rick Rubin and Celia Cruz. The ceremony was taped November 14th and airs December 8th on ABC and Disney+.

items.title: U2 Deliver Surprise Performance at 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony
items.summary:
U2 opened the 2026 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on Saturday at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles with an unannounced two-song set. The band played "Silencio," from its new album Carnaval De Luz, followed by "Pride (In the Name of Love)."

For the first song, Bono and the band shared the stage with a line of performers costumed as riot police carrying shields. U2 were not among this year's honorees — the group was inducted in 2005, its first year of eligibility — making the appearance a return visit rather than a homecoming.

Consequence reported that the performance came a day after Carnaval De Luz arrived and coincided with the band's 50th anniversary. The album closes with "Torn," a duet that features the final recorded vocal performance by Dolly Parton.

The 2026 class inducted Saturday includes Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Luther Vandross, Oasis, Phil Collins, Sade and Wu-Tang Clan, among others. A primetime special drawing on performances and highlights from the night airs December 8th from 8:00 to 11:00 p.m. ET on ABC, and streams on Disney+ the following day.

items.title: ‘SNL’: Watch Phoebe Bridgers Perform ‘Bobby,’ ‘Still Standing’
items.summary:
Phoebe Bridgers served as the musical guest on Saturday Night Live this weekend, playing two songs from her album Lost Weekend. She opened with "Bobby," a song about her relationship with comedian Bo Burnham, who co-wrote the track and sings on it.

Her second number was "Still Standing," which Bridgers wrote in response to the death of her father in 2023. The 16-song album also features contributions from her Boygenius bandmates Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus, along with Jack Antonoff and Geese frontman Cameron Winter.

As Rolling Stone noted, the record topped several charts, including Billboard's Independent Albums tally in the U.S. In the magazine's review, Angie Martoccio called it the 32-year-old songwriter's "longest and most daring record yet, a tour de force in the art of disappearing, falling in love, and feeling grief so deeply that waking up every day kind of sucks."

The appearance followed the release, a few days earlier, of Bridgers' Live at Madison Square Garden EP, which collects five songs from Lost Weekend. It was her third time on the SNL stage: she debuted in February 2021 with "Kyoto" and "I Know the End" from Punisher, and returned in November 2023 with Boygenius performing two songs from The Record.

Bridgers begins an eight-country European tour later this month behind Lost Weekend. The Lost Tour 2027 runs across North America from February through May, including two weekends at Coachella in April, and she headlines Iowa's three-day Hinterland Music Festival in late July.
